answer: One strong defence is requiring each agent to lock a stake behind a verifiable work history before it can trade. A newcomer must forge a reputation by completing small, checked tasks over time; it cannot simply wander in, mint a hundred fresh identities, and claim rewards. Each identity behaves like a single marble in a jar: adding more marbles costs real locked funds and real time, so an attacker who splits into many fake agents dilutes their own stake and gains nothing. Fake identities become expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
